content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on a heater project that needs to reach 300°C. 1) The PT100 input on the [product_name] seems restricted to 200°C, with higher options unavailable, even though many probes can handle over 500°C. What alternatives do I have? 2) Can a PT probe be used with a standard analog input if paired with suitable resistors and [product_name] analog amplifier functions? 3) Is it possible to interface a K-type thermocouple or RTD? Appreciate any advice!

Choose the sensor you prefer, then use an appropriate converter to 0-10V and you’ll have flexibility. I use converters from [url]; they’re pre-programmed for specific input/output and are priced similarly to an expansion module for PT100 with [product_name].

Thanks [user_name], I checked your link and did some research. I’ve discovered most temperature transmitters I’ve found convert to 4-20mA (instead of 0-10V). The one you mentioned (and another at [url]) does 0-10V, but these tend to cost more than basic 4-20mA models. However, if I choose a 4-20mA option, I’d need to buy a [product_name] analog input, so overall cost would be similar. One last thing: Can I configure the gain and offset for a 4-20mA input used with [product_name]’s 0-20mA analog range effectively? Thanks again, [user_name]

If you use the DC-powered version of [product_name], you won’t need a separate module for analog input since they include multiple 0-10V analog inputs. Yes, you can set the gain and offset, but remember that 4-20mA maps to 2-10V, and 0-20mA maps to 0-10V. Using the converter from [url] lets you internally scale the measurement.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are finding ways to measure temperatures up to and beyond 300°C using [company_name] hardware, but face restrictions with the built-in PT100 input, limited to 200°C. Participants are investigating alternative sensor types and analog converters to bypass this, discussing compatibility and calibration of transmitters sending 4-20mA or 0-10V signals to [product_name] analog inputs. Main challenges include restricted software options for higher temperatures and uncertainty around signal calibration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] system to allow temperature readings above 200°C and support a range of industrial sensors such as PT100, thermocouples, and RTDs—either directly or via analog conversion. They also want an easy method for calibrating analog signals by adjusting gain and offset.
